metadata.title: What survives? Semantic eligibility, distribution shift and metric interpretation in external validation of ADMET predictors

creators.name: Roktim, Md. Rahul Reza
creators.affiliation: Department of Pharmacy, Daffodil International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh

metadata.description: Analysis code, frozen result artefacts, figures, tables and manuscript for a study of assay-semantic eligibility in the external validation of ADMET predictors. A pre-specified, fail-closed screen of ten declared semantic gates was applied to twelve candidate pairings between three public experimental datasets and the outputs of ADMET-AI 2.0.1, before any metric was computed. Three pairings were accepted and nine rejected, each with a recorded reason; no classification endpoint qualified. On the accepted pairings, after excluding exact structure overlap with the endpoint training source and with the reconstructed regression multitask universe, external performance was R2 = -0.156 for human liver microsomal clearance (n = 366), 0.368 for logD at pH 7.4 (n = 474) and 0.642 for human plasma protein binding (n = 178). The model nevertheless outperformed training-mean and 1-nearest-neighbour baselines on every endpoint. Label-distribution shift (Kolmogorov-Smirnov D = 0.446 for clearance) and prediction-range compression (calibration slope 0.037; prediction standard deviation 9 percent of observed) account for the negative coefficient of determination, which therefore misrepresents model utility if reported alone. Reproduction is offered at two levels: Level 1 regenerates every reported number offline from committed redistributable artefacts; Level 2 documents how to obtain the upstream datasets and rebuild the reference tables that are deliberately not redistributed for licensing reasons.
